I farm only 5 mu, so I will keep the full wheat-maize rotation on all 5 mu instead of changing crops. That system fits my land, my experience, and my irrigation conditions, and it keeps the field busy for the whole year. Because some people in my family work off-farm, I will manage the land in a way that is steady and not too labor-intensive. For wheat, I will use improved seed, give enough base fertilizer plus topdressing, irrigate a few times with my well, and use rotary tillage because it is practical for my scale. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed because I care most about stable yield on limited land. I will keep fertilizer moderate but sufficient, irrigate when the crop needs it, and control pests with a small number of sprays rather than spraying too often. I am not chasing the highest possible yield; I will aim for a dependable yield with costs and labor kept under control.
